name: XSum
ability_definition: The ability to communicate information and ideas in writing so others will understand.

task_realism.reasoning: Condensing a news article into a single abstractive sentence resembles real tasks like writing a lede, headline-summary, or executive one-liner. The system must produce new prose that conveys a main idea. But it is one narrow task among the many workplace writing tasks (explaining, instructing, arguing, reporting, corresponding). There is also no specified audience or purpose beyond 'state the gist'.

evaluation_conditions.reasoning: Scoring is ROUGE overlap against a single reference. That reference is the article's own introductory sentence, which is noisy and often contains information absent from the body. No reader judges whether the output is understandable, clear, or accurate. Real written communication succeeds or fails on reader comprehension and fit to the audience, which ROUGE does not capture. Human evaluations have preferred lower-ROUGE outputs, so the metric can even anti-correlate with communicative quality.

construct_coverage.reasoning: It covers only one slice of Written Expression: compressing given content into one sentence in the news domain. It does not test organizing multi-paragraph text, choosing content for a purpose, adapting tone or register to different readers, argument, or instruction. It does not even test clarity as judged by readers. Faithfulness and correctness of what is conveyed are also poorly measured because of the noisy references.

format_match.reasoning: Inputs are genuine BBC news articles, and outputs are free-form natural-language sentences rather than multiple choice or structured labels. That is closer to real artifacts than many benchmarks. However, a fixed single-sentence output is a constrained format compared with typical workplace documents such as emails, reports, and explanations.

transferability_reasoning: XSum requires genuinely abstractive writing on real news text, which gives it some surface realism for Written Expression. It is restricted to one-sentence news summarization, though. More importantly, it is evaluated by n-gram overlap with a noisy single reference rather than by whether readers understand the text. Gains on XSum therefore say little about a system's ability to communicate information and ideas clearly to others in real work.

2022.human_reference: Relevant educated workforce: typical college-educated workers who routinely write short summaries or briefs of news or informational text as part of their jobs. This is not professional BBC sub-editors.
